units.function: End-to-end contract tests for Paperclip's OpenClaw WebSocket adapter and its configuration/parser surface, covering gateway challenge/connect, Agent submission, event streaming, result wait, runtime-service projection, environment checks and automatic device pairing.
units.dependencyDirection: Paperclip's server test imports the first-party OpenClaw adapter server and UI helpers through package exports, supplies an AdapterExecutionContext carrying Paperclip Agent/run/task/workspace/wake state, and exercises an in-process WebSocket gateway implementing the external protocol.
units.keyDataModels: AdapterExecutionContext; challenge and request/response/event WebSocket frames; protocol/server/features/snapshot/policy hello metadata; agent idempotencyKey/sessionKey/message; ordered stream delta event; wait result and runtimeServices metadata; structured gateway error; device pairing request; adapter result/errorCode; UI adapter configuration.
units.lifecycle: Gateway challenges the client; client connects with device/auth configuration; it submits a run using the Paperclip run ID as idempotency key and issue as session key; assistant events become logs/summary; agent.wait returns terminal metadata; pairing-required may trigger one automatic list/approve/reconnect attempt; environment validation reports missing URL before execution.
units.testAssessment: All seven tests pass outside the network-restricted sandbox. The fixtures give useful protocol-level coverage of handshake, structured gateway errors, idempotent submission, streaming order, wait completion, runtime-service projection and a retryable pairing path. Coverage is incomplete for incompatible protocol/features, authentication rejection and secret redaction, reconnect/resume/replay and duplicate sequence handling, cancellation, effective timeout behavior, retry budgets/backoff, approval pause/resume, evidence/result schemas, attestation, URL/network policy and payload-size enforcement.
units.designRationale: Provide an external Agent execution adapter that can retain a remote issue session, receive structured wake context, stream output and expose adapter-managed runtime services while automating first-use gateway device pairing.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a vendor-neutral Connector contract for Raft Agent, Codex, DeepSeek, enterprise Agents and later runtimes, with capability/version negotiation, identity binding, health, idempotent task execution, progress, cancellation, timeout, risk approval suspension, evidence/results and secret-free run proof.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the executable WebSocket contract-test pattern and stable structured error handling, not Paperclip's context or wire payload. Define a Company OS Connector SDK with explicit version/capability negotiation; opaque work/contract/principal IDs; separately scoped identity and credential references; submit/status/event/resume/cancel APIs; monotonic sequence and replay cursor; idempotency and concurrency tokens; bounded retry/timeout policy; digest-bound approval suspension/resume; typed evidence/result manifests; short-lived secret-free runtime attestation; health and network-policy declarations. Translate Company OS projections at the adapter edge and redact all secrets and private provider sessions.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tested run can begin after gateway device pairing without a Company OS accountable-human contract or action-digest approval. The message embeds Paperclip-specific work and wake context, while output is summarized from assistant deltas rather than bound to typed evidence/result and permission/data-use records. Automatic pairing approval also conflates technical device trust with organizational authorization.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: missing configuration returns a stable code; gateway errors are structured; submissions use an idempotency key; feature/policy metadata exists; a former product-root payload is asserted absent. CRITICAL responsibility gap for Company OS: device pairing is automatically approved and is not equivalent to accountable-human authorization of an Agent, permission scope or high-risk action. HIGH credential boundary gap: tests put a raw gateway token in adapter config and do not prove vault references, log redaction, rotation or audience isolation. HIGH execution-contract gap: no approval suspension/resume, cancellation, typed evidence/results, data-authorization record or digest-bound responsibility chain. HIGH network gap: arbitrary ws/wss URL behavior is not tested against SSRF, allowlists, TLS or egress policy. MEDIUM resilience gap: no protocol/capability rejection, reconnect/replay/deduplication, timeout/retry-budget or out-of-order sequence tests. MEDIUM minimization gap: rich comments, workspace and runtime details are embedded into a provider-facing text message without a tested disclosure policy.
